title: A function toolkit
description:
Build a small library of tools that wrap other functions, the kind every larger Lua program ends up with. Write them as fields of a module table and return it:

```lua-norun
local fn = {}
-- ...
return fn
```

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `fn.memoize(f)` | a function like `f` (one argument) that calls `f` only once per different argument, and gives the remembered result after that, even when the result is `nil` or `false` |
| `fn.once(f)` | a function that calls `f` the first time (with its arguments, returning all its results) and afterwards returns those same results without calling `f` |
| `fn.partial(f, ...)` | a function that calls `f` with the given arguments first, followed by its own arguments |
| `fn.pipe(...)` | a function that passes its argument through every given function from left to right; with no functions it returns its argument unchanged |
| `fn.count_calls(f)` | two results: a function that calls `f` and passes back all its results, and a function that returns how many times it has been called |

```lua-norun
local add = function(a, b, c) return a + b + (c or 0) end
fn.partial(add, 1)(2)              --> 3
fn.partial(add, 1, 2)(3)           --> 6
fn.pipe(math.abs, math.sqrt)(-16)  --> 4.0
```
hints: To remember a `nil` result, a table of results alone is not enough (`cache[x] = nil` stores nothing). Keep a second table that records which arguments have been seen.
`table.pack(...)` keeps every value and the count `n`, nils included; `table.unpack(t, 1, t.n)` gives them all back.
requirements: memoize calls the wrapped function once per argument, also when it returns nil or false.
once returns every result of the first call, every time.
partial and pipe pass arguments through in the right order.
count_calls counts and passes results through.
stretch: - Let `memoize` work for functions of several arguments, by building a key from all of them.
unitTests:
test("memoize remembers each argument", function()
    local calls = 0
    local slow_square = function(x) calls = calls + 1; return x * x end
    local fast = solution.memoize(slow_square)
    check_eq(fast(4), 16)
    check_eq(fast(4), 16)
    check_eq(fast(5), 25)
    check_eq(calls, 2)
end)

test("memoize remembers nil and false too", function()
    local calls = 0
    local lookup = function(k) calls = calls + 1; if k == "no" then return false end return nil end
    local m = solution.memoize(lookup)
    check_eq(m("no"), false)
    check_eq(m("no"), false)
    check_eq(m("missing"), nil)
    check_eq(m("missing"), nil)
    check_eq(calls, 2)
end)

test("once", function()
    local calls = 0
    local init = solution.once(function(a, b) calls = calls + 1; return a + b, "ready" end)
    check_eq({ init(1, 2) }, { 3, "ready" })
    check_eq({ init(10, 20) }, { 3, "ready" })
    check_eq(calls, 1)
end)

test("partial", function()
    local add = function(a, b, c) return a + b + (c or 0) end
    check_eq(solution.partial(add, 1)(2), 3)
    check_eq(solution.partial(add, 1, 2)(3), 6)
    check_eq(solution.partial(string.rep, "ab")(3), "ababab")
    local both = function(a, b) return tostring(a) .. "," .. tostring(b) end
    check_eq(solution.partial(both, nil)("x"), "nil,x")
end)

test("pipe", function()
    check_eq(solution.pipe(math.abs, math.sqrt)(-16), 4.0)
    check_eq(solution.pipe(string.upper, string.reverse, function(s) return s .. "!" end)("abc"), "CBA!")
    check_eq(solution.pipe()(7), 7)
end)

test("count_calls", function()
    local wrapped, count = solution.count_calls(function(a, b) return b, a end)
    check_eq(count(), 0)
    check_eq({ wrapped(1, 2) }, { 2, 1 })
    wrapped(3, 4)
    check_eq(count(), 2)
end)
